title: Postpartum checkup
what: A visit to the gynecologist after giving birth. The doctor checks how your body is recovering and answers your questions.
why: For everyone after birth, usually at 6 to 8 weeks. Sooner if something bothers you.
duration: the visit usually takes 20 to 40 minutes
tell_doctor: What your bleeding or discharge is like now, and how much
Leaking urine or trouble going to the toilet
Your mood: sadness, anxiety, sleeplessness. This is important to mention
If you are breastfeeding, and what medicines you take

prepare.title: Questions
prepare.text: Write down your questions: birth control, sex, exercise, feeding.

prepare.title: Your baby
prepare.text: Ask if you can bring your baby, or arrange for someone to watch them.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Sometimes a blood or urine test is needed. Your doctor will say.

steps: The doctor asks how you feel, physically and emotionally
Your belly and breasts are examined
A pelvic exam is done, and any stitches are checked
Birth control and returning to activity are discussed
feel: The pelvic exam may be uncomfortable, especially if you had stitches
after: If all is well, your doctor will clear you for sex and exercise, little by little
Choose birth control. You can get pregnant even while breastfeeding
Pelvic floor exercises help you recover
red_flags: Heavy bleeding that soaks a pad in an hour: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or bad-smelling discharge
A painful, red, hard area in the breast with a fever
Thoughts of harming yourself or your baby: call emergency services right away

faq.q: When can I have sex after giving birth?
faq.a: Usually once the bleeding has stopped and your doctor has checked you. Often around 6 weeks.

faq.q: Can I get pregnant while breastfeeding?
faq.a: Yes, you can. Think about birth control early and talk to your doctor.

faq.q: I feel sad all the time. Is that normal?
faq.a: Mood swings are common in the first days. If the sadness lasts more than 2 weeks, tell your doctor. It can be treated.

reminders.text: Postpartum checkup tomorrow. Bring your hospital discharge papers and write down your questions.
